roofing.title: From worn shingles to a renewed roof
roofing.description: Compare an aged shingle roof with a complete roof replacement. The roof covering, ridge and flashing are the visible changes in this example.

before.alt: Illustration: Aged asphalt shingles on a brick home

after.alt: Illustration: New charcoal architectural shingles on the same brick home

roof-repair.title: A focused repair at the chimney
roof-repair.description: This example keeps the surrounding roof in place while replacing damaged shingles and correcting the flashing at the chimney. A repair should address the affected connection as well as the visible covering.

before.alt: Illustration: Missing shingles and deteriorated chimney flashing

after.alt: Illustration: Matching shingle repair and renewed chimney flashing

metal-roofing.title: From shingles to standing-seam metal
metal-roofing.description: The same roofline takes on a different character with standing-seam metal. Compare the long panel seams, ridge and edge trim with the shingle covering they replace.

before.alt: Illustration: Weathered shingle roof on a white farmhouse

after.alt: Illustration: Charcoal standing-seam metal roof on the same farmhouse

commercial-roofing.title: A renewed commercial roof covering
commercial-roofing.description: Compare a worn low-slope covering with a new membrane and finished curb details. Equipment, outlets and the building stay in place; the roof assembly needs its own assessment before replacement.

before.alt: Illustration: Aged commercial membrane with worn seams and shallow ponding

after.alt: Illustration: New light-gray membrane with finished curb flashing

commercial-repair.title: Repairing a membrane seam and curb
commercial-repair.description: A localized membrane repair can address an open seam and deteriorated curb flashing while retaining sound surrounding material. The patch and its connections should match the selected roof system.

before.alt: Illustration: Split membrane and loose flashing at an equipment curb

after.alt: Illustration: Localized membrane patch and repaired curb flashing

siding.title: From damaged courses to a finished exterior
siding.description: The comparison shows displaced siding replaced with a complete, neatly trimmed wall covering. Corners and window edges matter alongside the panel color and profile.

before.alt: Illustration: Buckled tan siding with a small area of exposed housewrap

after.alt: Illustration: Slate-blue lap siding with finished corners and window trim

commercial-siding.title: Restoring the commercial facade
commercial-siding.description: New wall panels and matching opening trim replace weathered, damaged cladding in this example. The same doors and windows remain, making the change in the wall surface easy to compare.

before.alt: Illustration: Weathered commercial metal siding with damaged lower panels

after.alt: Illustration: Renewed charcoal commercial metal siding and opening trim

gutters.title: A straighter run and a finished outlet
gutters.description: Compare an aged gutter corner with a replacement run and a neatly connected downspout. The installation still needs the right support, slope and discharge route for the building.

before.alt: Illustration: Sagging stained gutter corner and imperfect downspout connection

after.alt: Illustration: Straight white gutter run with finished corner and downspout

gutter-guards.title: From an open gutter to a screened opening
gutter-guards.description: This example shows debris removed and a fine-mesh guard fitted above the gutter. Guards address debris entry; they do not replace sound gutters, downspouts or routine inspection.

before.alt: Illustration: Leaves and twigs collected in an open gutter

after.alt: Illustration: Fine-mesh gutter guard above the same cleaned gutter

commercial-gutters.title: Renewing a commercial gutter and outlet
commercial-gutters.description: The replacement gutter and rectangular downspout form a connected rainwater route. Compare the run, outlet and attachments; capacity and discharge still depend on the building.

before.alt: Illustration: Weathered commercial box gutter and rust-streaked outlet

after.alt: Illustration: Renewed charcoal box gutter and aligned rectangular downspout

decks.title: A new walking surface and railing
decks.description: Compare weathered timber decking with a replacement surface, fascia and railing in the same footprint. Framing, ledger connections and stairs need assessment before a similar project is planned.

before.alt: Illustration: Weathered timber deck boards, stairs and railing

after.alt: Illustration: Warm-brown replacement deck surface with charcoal railing

deck-refinishing.title: The same timber, with a renewed finish
deck-refinishing.description: The boards and railing stay in place in this example. Cleaning, preparation and a fresh wood finish change the appearance; refinishing does not replace structurally damaged timber.

before.alt: Illustration: Faded timber boards with a worn finish

after.alt: Illustration: The same timber boards with a renewed cedar-brown finish

deck-repair.title: Replacing the damaged boards, retaining the rest
deck-repair.description: A focused board repair leaves the surrounding deck in place. The underlying supports and connections should also be checked wherever decay or movement is found.

before.alt: Illustration: Split and decayed board ends beside a deck step

after.alt: Illustration: Sound replacement timber in the affected board locations

deck-accessories.title: Adding light to steps and railing posts
deck-accessories.description: Post-cap and stair lighting can help define the deck after dark. Plan the fixture positions, wiring routes and compatible power components with the deck layout.

before.alt: Illustration: Deck steps and railing without fitted lighting

after.alt: Illustration: The same deck with warm post-cap and stair lighting

windows.title: Renewed frames and clearer glazing
windows.description: The same window openings receive replacement units and finished perimeter trim. Compare the frames and glass; installation details around the opening remain part of the work.

before.alt: Illustration: Weathered wood window frames and a fogged glass pane

after.alt: Illustration: White replacement windows with clear glazing and finished trim

insulation.title: A more continuous layer across the attic floor
insulation.description: The example shows thin, uneven insulation replaced by a deeper, continuous floor layer. Air sealing, ventilation paths and access need to be considered with the insulation work.

before.alt: Illustration: Thin uneven attic-floor insulation with exposed joist tops

after.alt: Illustration: A deeper continuous insulation layer with ventilation paths retained

ice-dam.title: Clearing the ice ridge at the roof edge
ice-dam.description: The thick refrozen ridge in the first image restricts the roof-edge drainage path. The second shows that ridge removed while snow remains upslope. Removal and the causes of recurring ice buildup are separate parts of the assessment.

before.alt: Illustration: Thick ice dam extending onto shingles above the gutter

after.alt: Illustration: The same roof edge after the ice ridge is cleared

painting.title: A fresh finish on the same wood siding
painting.description: Preparation and a renewed coating change the exterior without replacing the cladding. Compare the painted boards and window trim; damaged wood needs repair before finishing.

before.alt: Illustration: Faded green painted wood siding with peeling finish

after.alt: Illustration: The same wood siding painted ivory with charcoal trim

wind-damage.title: Restoring the wind-damaged shingle courses
wind-damage.description: The example shows missing and lifted tabs replaced with matching shingles. An inspection documents the affected materials and checks the surrounding roof before repair recommendations are made.

before.alt: Illustration: Lifted and missing shingle tabs beside a dormer

after.alt: Illustration: Matching repaired shingle courses beside the same dormer

hail-damage.title: Replacing the affected shingles and vent
hail-damage.description: Compare the visibly affected shingle surface and vent hood with replacement materials. This illustration explains a repair; photographs of the actual property are needed to document observed damage.

before.alt: Illustration: Granule-loss impact spots and a dented metal vent hood

after.alt: Illustration: Replacement shingles and an undented matching vent hood
